title: Derive custom inference KPIs and OTLP span label enrichment for cardinality-controlled metrics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current Prometheus/OTel pipeline emits high-cardinality labels (model_id, route_id, prompt_hash buckets, user_id variants) that make long-term KPI storage and alerts impractical. We need a controlled, derivation-layer that produces stable, low-cardinality inference KPIs derived from spans and raw metrics while preserving useful routing/model context for debugging.

Goals:
- Enrich OTLP traces/spans with normalized, low-cardinality labels suitable for Prometheus and our KPI backends (e.g., model_family, model_variant_bucket, route_group).
- Derive new metrics (exported as inference_kpi_* Prometheus metrics) such as per-model p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_second (per-route), kv_cache_hit_ratio (prefix-length buckets), and evictions_per_minute aggregated at model_family level.
- Implement cardinality reduction strategies: mapping tables, label bucketing, deterministic hashing with controlled namespaces, and sampled high-cardinality tags for debugging-only pipelines.
- Maintain linkability: keep span.trace_id and an opaque debug_tag in a high-cardinality trace store (retention 7d) so on-call can pivot from a KPI alert to the full trace without blowing up metric cardinality.

Design decisions & trade-offs (summary):
- Enrichment location: will perform label normalization in the OTLP processing layer (collector pipeline) before metrics conversion. This keeps relabel rules out of Prometheus and enables richer derivations (e.g., compute tokens/sec by dividing token_count metric by compute_time).
- Cardinality approach: prefer deterministic bucketing + mapping table for model_id -> model_family to keep label space stable. Use sampled debug-export path to retain full model_id/user_id for 0.1% of requests.
- KPI computation: implement derived time-series in the exporter (collector) to emit inference_kpi_{latency,p95,tokens_per_sec,kv_hit_ratio,evictions} with consistent label set {region, deployment_tier, model_family, route_group}.
- Backfill/backcompat: export legacy metrics for 30d and provide conversion mapping in BigQuery for historical comparisons.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- New metrics appear in staging Prometheus with correct label set and cardinality < 10k labels across all clusters.
- Alerts for p95 latency at model_family level trigger within 1m of condition and link to a Grafana panel that includes the debug-sampled trace list.
- E2E tests (telemetry-tests repo) validate mapping table updates and sampled debug path.
- PRs reviewed and merged for collector config, exporter code, and Prometheus relabel snippets where needed.

Implementation plan (high level):
1. Create collector enrichment module: normalize model_id -> model_family, bucketize latency and prefix_length, and inject debug_tag on sampled traces. (Diego)
2. Implement derived KPI generator in the collector exporter that calculates rates and ratios across spans/metrics windows (1m, 5m). (Diego + telemetry eng)
3. Add deterministic hashing helpers and mapping table CRD (config repo) to keep bucketing consistent across regions. (Infra)
4. Wire new metrics to staging Prometheus and create Grafana dashboards. (Observability)
5. Add integration tests and a migration plan for legacy metrics. (QA)

2026-02-18 - Diego Marquez: Prototype collector enrichment completed. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector-enrichment/pull/7. Key change: model_id -> model_family mapping file and prefix_length buckets implemented. Needs performance bench on 10k rps.

2026-02-22 - Priya Singh (Observability): Dashboard prototype added: grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-kpi/inference-kpi-overview?orgId=1. Confirmed label set works for region/deployment_tier/model_family. Still seeing one high-cardinality label from "raw_prompt_sig"; we decided to drop it at collector level.

2026-02-25 - Diego Marquez: Load test on staging (12k rps) shows CPU increase of 7% in collector workers with enrichment enabled. Trade-off accepted; will add autoscaling policy for collector workers and enable sampling of debug exports at 0.1%.

2026-03-03 - Security review thread: security@redwood.co reviewed debug_tag retention plan; approved with retention TTL 7d and KMS encryption for the debug-store. No change required to customer-visible labels.

2026-03-08 - QA: integration tests added in telemetry-tests (https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-tests/compare/feature/kpi-enrichment). Tests cover bucketization and tokens/sec computation across windows. Flaky case found for KV cache hit ratio when prefix_length=0; QA created follow-up ENG-35699.

2026-03-12 - Diego Marquez: Ready for In Review. Code PRs: collector changes https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector-enrichment/pull/14, exporter changes https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-exporter/pull/88. Please review by 2026-03-16.
next_steps: Finish code review and merge PRs, enable staged rollout to us-west-2, monitor cardinality and CPU, then flip staging->prod after 48h with no cardinality regressions.
notes: This ticket focuses on telemetry pipeline changes only. Runtime changes to emit additional base metrics (token_count, kv_events) are tracked in ENG-36102. If mapping table updates are required during rollout, follow mapping table change process in obs-config README.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy collector enrichment in staging and validate metrics. 2) Migrate legacy metric consumers by toggling feature flag for derived metrics for 7 days. 3) Remove legacy high-cardinality metrics from exporter after 30 days. 4) Backfill historical KPIs via BigQuery conversion script (stored in obs-bq-scripts repo).
